author: s2eh

title: Do not get this app!
body:
After following an ad on Instagram targeted at helping someone with ADHD improve their habits and routines I decided to give Habio a go and signed up for a 3-day for €5.49. €5.49 seemed like a reasonable amount to see if the app could fulfil on the promises made in the advertising and offer.

However, after the trial offer was accepted, a screen with a large brightly coloured button saying ‘Get my PDF workbook’ appears. As someone with ADHD, I made the mistake of impulsively clicking on the button without stopping to read the surrounding text.

I immediately realised my mistake when I was taken to a screen that told me I had been charged an extra $29.99 for the ebook. Because my intention was only to go for the trial to test the app, not purchase a $29.99 ebook (which I would most likely never read) I didn’t click on the link to download the ebook and got in touch with the Habio helpdesk to explain my mistake and ask for a refund.

I thought it was a reasonable request, especially as I had contacted them the moment I realised my mistake and, more importantly, hadn’t given my consent for the extra charge. At least that’s what I thought. 

Upon contacting the Habio support I was told there was a strict no refund policy and that I had given my permission via the terms and conditions and that all the information was readily available on the PDF purchase screen. After they provided screenshots of the offer pages it became clear that this offer is only designed to trick someone into clicking on the more expensive upsell PDF button.

On review of the ‘Special Offer’ screen, all the important information, such as price and consent to the extra charge, are in a type size and colour designed to blend with the background, making it almost illegible on a quick scan of the page. The consent to charge text is in such a low contrast colour with the background, and such a tiny type size that it hurts my eyes to even read it!

It feels as though this page has been designed with the intent of tricking the very type of person that they claim to want to help into making a purchase that on quick glance would appear to be a PDF attached to the trial offer you’ve agreed to, without clear extra charge.

Very disappointed that there are companies out there like Habio trying to take advantage of underhanded sales tactics rather than genuinely wanting to help and make a positive difference in the world.

title: Waste of £30
body:
Firstly this app doesn’t offer a free trial so you have to commit from the outset. I opted for the best value of £27.99 for the year as the app and the reviews seemed good.
It was a downhill slide from there unfortunately.

The app is seriously buggy.
View settings often don’t work and endless tapping to move through screens because it hangs constantly.
There is no option to ‘ignore’ certain features and takes you round and round in loops until you select something that you never wanted in the first place. For instance I want to record a habit but don’t necessarily want to log one of their options for reward such as listen to a song or eat a piece of fruit (seriously who devised these?) but it will prompt you to death until you go through the motions.

With the habit tracking itself I’d like the option to say I’d like to do something x-times a week. The set up on this is you have to say which days you’ll do it. Thanks, but life doesn’t always work like that and I’d just like to know that I achieved my commitment of number of days.

The journal is yet another prompt based system so pre-defined responses with some free text but not very intuitive. Want to include a photo in your journal?  Nope sorry that feature doesn’t exist.
Want to see your achievements in calendar view? No sorry can’t do that either.

Want to log in on your iPad? You can but only once you’ve worked through the entire initial set up process all over again. Seriously developers just add a log in option at the beginning!!

There are some nice articles and short reads on wellbeing topics included which is the best part of this app but not necessarily what people are coming here for.  If this is what you were coming here for I’d suggest you save yourself the cash and take a look at the wellbeing section on apple news.

I’ve already cancelled the subscription so I don’t forget and it renews in a years time, but I’m beyond disappointed with the usability of the app and endless prompts that extend into being seriously irritating.

If you’re a person incapable of thinking for yourself then this is probably for you. For everyone else you’ll feel like you’re being treated like an idiot and irritated by needless and unwanted options that you didn’t ask for.

title: Amazing
body: Hi I’m Daisy I struggle to stay on track and my goals usually last less than a week. I keep meaning to download an app but they all cost money which is a bit of a pain but the fact this app was free really motivated me I’ve been doing so well with my goals and it was really funny because I was scrolling through Instagram and I saw an ad for this app so it must have been a sign telling me to be organised 😂
author: golprew
